cases.name: edited-one-harness
cases.prompt: I just edited the run-e2e SKILL.md under .cursor/skills to fix a typo. Anything else I need to do before I commit?
cases.why: The everyday case. The user never says 'sync' or 'drift' — they describe editing one harness and ask what is left, which is exactly the moment M5 bites. If the description only catches people who already know the rule, it is useless to the person who does not.

cases.name: gate-6d-red
cases.prompt: sweep just failed on 6d. sort it out for me
cases.why: Rewritten after the first real run. The original was 'sweep just failed on 6d, what is that' - a definition lookup, which the model answered correctly and completely from the repo without consulting anything. That is the documented behaviour, not a description gap: a skill is consulted for work the model cannot already do in one step, so a case phrased as a lookup tests nothing about triggering. The real situation behind those words is someone whose gate is red who wants it fixed, and that needs the skill's repair procedure - which direction to propagate, and never to satisfy the gate by deleting the change.

cases.name: settings-json-differs
cases.prompt: my .cursor/settings.json and .claude/settings.json have totally different contents. can you make them match?
cases.why: The near-miss that matters. Same directories, same word 'match', and it looks like drift — but settings.json is harness-specific and making the three identical would break two harnesses. A description broad enough to catch 'the folders differ' will wrongly claim this one, and the skill would then advise a destructive sync.
